verification.notes: Draft: no DfE, Ofqual or school reviewer has checked this pack. Source links: the four gov.uk URLs and the UCAS URL all resolved to the named pages on 2026-10-21 (titles matched); the UCAS Tariff table itself is rendered client-side and was not read off the live page, so the per-grade tariff in this pack is taken from platform spec 03 Appendix C and still needs checking against the published table. The tariff is per grade, not per grade and subject: a candidate's total is the sum over the A levels taken. What is a placeholder, not a claim: the gcse_9_1 and alevel_a_star_e percentage bands. Ofqual sets grade boundaries per subject and per exam series after marking, and the A* is awarded by a subject-level rule above the A boundary, so no fixed percentage-to-grade table exists; both scales are declared overridable (grading_scales.<code>.bands) and a school must replace them with the board's boundaries for each session. The primary and key stage 3 attainment levels are a school rubric because England has had no statutory level scale since 2015. What is structured but unverified: the GCSE paper counts and maxima (English two papers of 80; mathematics three papers of 80) follow the published GCSE subject structures but were not read from a specification PDF in this environment; A level subjects declare no papers, and the Mathematics A level paper set is not modelled, because the pack declares only the GCSE papers at Y10-Y11 and no A level paper maxima were verified. Grade codes are the printed grades, so A* is the band code and the label repeats it. Calendar: the pack declares both the northern (September) and the southern (January) academic year as named variants, with the northern one as default, as spec 03 Appendix C asks. Year 2 SATs are not modelled as a national assessment because they became non-statutory; Year 12 has none because AS levels are decoupled and optional.
